experiment: Controlled comparison: CroW vs. Web Scraper (Chrome/Firefox extension, webscraper.io)
motivation: Addresses Bioinformatics Advances Reviewer 1's claim of successfully extracting UniProt entry pages and ClinicalTrials.gov search results with Web Scraper.
methodology: Identical target pages and fields on both systems. CroW run through the real production engine (_run_scraping_async). Web Scraper operated manually by the paper's author (browser automation could not reach it -- DevTools/extensions gallery are blocked from scripting, confirmed directly). All Web Scraper exports scored with the same scoring logic as the main 141-resource benchmark (compute_metrics.py's score_list_mode / score_single_page_mode).

web_scraper.reuse: first build, not a reuse test

FAILED: editing/reusing the existing sitemap's start URL did not work (0 records scraped); required building a new sitemap, which the AI Wizard auto-named with different, non-semantic columns (data/data2/...) than the first run
Also required a fresh sitemap (yet a third distinct auto-generated column layout observed across the three runs)

web_scraper_ai_wizard.failure_mode: AI Wizard auto-detected and scraped the page's Natural Variant feature table (70 rows) instead of the single-entity header fields (ProteinName/GeneName/Organism/Status)
Same failure mode, different wrong table: Natural Variant + Mutagenesis feature table
Same failure mode, a third distinct wrong table: the sequence/EMBL-GenBank cross-reference table (85 rows)

web_scraper_manual_spot_check.result: SUCCESS -- manually clicking the protein name text produced a correct single-value CSS selector (.info-list--columns li:nth-of-type(1) strong) returning exactly "Cellular tumor antigen p53". Not scraped/exported/scored as a full record; this is a targeted spot-check confirming manual point-and-click selection can correctly target this page, isolating the AI Wizard's auto-detection specifically as the point of failure, not manual Web Scraper use in general.

summary.tier0: Both systems reach 100%/100% on all three ClinicalTrials.gov queries (record-level NCT ID matching), at comparable per-query execution time (~4-5s). CroW's wrapper was reused unchanged across all three queries with no reconfiguration. Web Scraper's sitemap reuse did not work as expected (editing the stored start URL produced 0 records); each query effectively required a new sitemap, and the AI Wizard's auto-generated column names were not consistent across runs.
summary.tier1: CroW reaches 100%/100% on all three UniProt entry pages, the same unmodified wrapper reused across all three (~12s each). Web Scraper's AI Wizard failed all three (0%/0%), each time auto-detecting a different wrong repeating table on the page instead of the single-entity header fields. A manual spot-check on one field (protein name, P04637) confirmed Web Scraper's manual point-and-click selection can correctly target the right element -- the failure is specific to the AI-assisted auto-detection step, not an inherent inability of the tool to address Tier 1 pages by hand.

fairness_notes: Automated cloud scraping ('Automate in Cloud') was never used -- a paid tier explicitly excluded to keep the comparison to Web Scraper's free, local functionality, matching what CroW uses.
All runs used the same target pages, fields, and ground truth as the main 141-resource benchmark; no new ground truth was fetched.

Browser automation could not operate Web Scraper directly (confirmed: the extensions gallery and DevTools are both blocked from scripting), so Web Scraper was operated manually by the paper's author throughout; CroW ran through its real, unmodified production engine.
